words-only.why: I checked each of the 7 verifier checks against its expect line. Checks 1–5 compare the output byte for byte with cmp against the exact expected text plus a newline. Only check 1 also requires exit=0, which its line demands. Check 5 keeps the JSON backslash-t literal with printf '%s', matching the line. Check 6 PASS needs npm test to exit 0 and a test in test/ that runs bin/csv2json.js with --tsv on tab input and asserts on the output. Its FAIL examples (comment-only, no tabs, no assertion) only spell out those words. Check 7 needs an example --tsv invocation and that README "documents what the flag does", which is a fair reading of "documents the --tsv flag with an example invocation". `table.tsv` appears only "for example", not as required wording. The stricter ideas (flag position, whether the tests catch removed --tsv handling, out-of-scope changes) all sit under "Advisory (does not affect PASS or FAIL)".

runs-as-written.why: All commands would run as written. They use bin/csv2json.js, test/*.js and README.md, which all exist, and `npm test` maps to the existing "node --test" script. The briefs avoid the issue's nonexistent `npm run test:cli`. The builder's `printf ... | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv; echo "exit=$?"` lines are valid shell, and $? gives node's exit status. The verifier's `printf '%s\n' '...' | cmp - /tmp/vN.out && echo MATCH` is valid; `cmp -` reads stdin. In check 5, single quotes plus %s keep the literal backslash-t that the JSON output has. `grep -n -- '--tsv' test/*.js` and `README.md` take their arguments correctly. The JS escaping hint `[{"a\\tb":"1\\t2"}]\n` is valid JS string syntax. No syntax or argument errors found.

catches-traps.why:
I checked both must_catch items, and both are handled.

Item 1: The builder brief names test/csv.test.js and says it "has a `cli` test". Step 2 says to add the new tests there "or a new file in test/" and to "Keep the existing tests". Step 4 requires `npm test` to exit 0, so the existing CSV tests have to keep passing. Step 1 also protects the CSV path: without the flag the CLI calls "`parse(text)` exactly as now", and the brief says not to change src/parse.js unless needed.

Item 2: Verifier Check 6 runs `npm test; echo "exit=$?"`, as line 6 says. It does not use proof 6's undefined `npm run test:cli`.

So the output handles everything on the must_catch list.

avoids-must-not.why: I checked both items on the must_not list, and neither brief does either one. (1) Verifier Check 6 bases PASS/FAIL on "npm test; echo \"exit=$?\"" and a grep of test/*.js. `npm run test:cli` doesn't appear anywhere in either brief, even though the issue's proof uses it. No other check depends on it. (2) The builder brief never asks for a general separator option. It only checks for `--tsv` in process.argv and calls `parse(text, '\t')`. It names "a general --sep/--delimiter option" only under "Out of scope." The verifier mentions --sep/--delimiter only in an advisory note that says to flag such an option as an out-of-scope change.

methods-private.why: The builder brief has no PASS/FAIL wording and none of the verifier's probes. The verifier's `cmp`-against-expected scripts, the `/tmp/vN.out` captures, `grep -n -- '--tsv' test/*.js` and `grep -n -- '--tsv' README.md` are all missing from it. The builder's step 4 runs only the expect-line commands (e.g. `printf 'a\tb\n1\t2\n' | node bin/csv2json.js --tsv; echo "exit=$?"`) and `npm test; echo "exit=$?"`. The expect lines and proofs name all of these, so they are allowed. Step 2 tells the builder to write its own tests on the expect-line inputs, which is allowed. The README instruction (`node bin/csv2json.js --tsv < table.tsv`, plus saying the flag means tab-separated input) repeats issue proof 7. It is the bar for the work, not a verifier check. The advisory probes (flag not first, mutation check) are absent from the builder brief.
